result.topic_en: Derivation that in coordinates built from shortest lines (geodesic/normal coordinates) through the point 0, the metric coefficients satisfy Σ a_{μι} x_ι = Σ a^{(0)}_{μι} x_ι, using homogeneity arguments; it begins a lemma on quadratic forms vanishing identically.
result.transcription:
22.
Linien in die neuen Variabeln ein, so ergiebt sich:
$d \sum_\iota a_{\mu,\iota} x_\iota = \frac{1}{2} dr \sum_{\iota,\iota'} \frac{\partial a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_\mu} x_\iota x_{\iota'}$,
woraus folgt:
(3.) $\sum_{\iota\iota'} p_{\mu,\iota,\iota'} x_\iota x_{\iota'} = 0$,
wenn zur Abkürzung gesetzt ist:
$p_{\mu,\iota,\iota'} = \frac{\partial a_{\iota\mu}}{\partial x_{\iota'}} + \frac{\partial a_{\iota'\mu}}{\partial x_\iota} - \frac{\partial a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_\mu}$.
Die Gleichung (3.) läßt sich auch so schreiben:
(3'.) $\sum_{\iota\iota'} \frac{\partial a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_\mu} x_\iota x_{\iota'} = 2 \sum_{\iota\iota'} \frac{\partial a_{\iota\mu}}{\partial x_{\iota'}} x_\iota x_{\iota'}$.
Setzen wir nun zur Abkürzung:
$\omega_\mu = \sum_\iota a_{\mu,\iota} x_\iota$; $\frac{\partial \omega_\mu}{\partial x_\nu} = a_{\mu,\nu} + \sum_\iota \frac{\partial a_{\mu,\iota}}{\partial x_\nu} x_\iota$,
so läßt sich die Gleichung (3') so schreiben:
$\omega_\mu + \sum_\iota \frac{\partial \omega_\iota}{\partial x_\mu} x_\iota = 2 \sum_\iota \frac{\partial \omega_\mu}{\partial x_\iota} x_\iota$.
Setzt man ferner
$2\omega = \sum_\iota \omega_\iota x_\iota$; $2 \frac{\partial \omega}{\partial x_\mu} = \omega_\mu + \sum_\iota \frac{\partial \omega_\iota}{\partial x_\mu} x_\iota$,
so folgt hieraus:
$\frac{\partial \omega}{\partial x_\mu} = \sum_\iota \frac{\partial \omega_\mu}{\partial x_\iota} x_\iota$; $\frac{\partial^2 \omega}{\partial x_\mu \partial x_\nu} = \frac{\partial \omega_\mu}{\partial x_\nu} + \sum_\iota \frac{\partial^2 \omega_\mu}{\partial x_\iota \partial x_\nu} x_\iota$,
und hieraus:
$\frac{\partial \omega_\mu}{\partial x_\nu} - \frac{\partial \omega_\nu}{\partial x_\mu} + \sum_\iota \frac{\partial}{\partial x_\iota}\left(\frac{\partial \omega_\mu}{\partial x_\nu} - \frac{\partial \omega_\nu}{\partial x_\mu}\right) x_\iota$
woraus hervorgeht, daß die $\frac{\partial \omega_\mu}{\partial x_\nu} - \frac{\partial \omega_\nu}{\partial x_\mu}$ homogene
Functionen der (-1)ten Ordnung sind. Bezeichnet man
eine solche mit $f(x_1, x_2, \ldots x_n)$, so hat man:
$f(tx_1, tx_2, \ldots tx_n) = t^{-1} f(x_1, x_2, \ldots x_n)$.
Setzt man daher voraus, daß die Coefficienten $a_{\iota\iota'}$
und ihre Ableitungen im Punkte 0 bestimmte endliche Werthe haben, so folgt, wenn man
$t=0$ setzt, daß die Function f identisch verschwinden
muß, daß also $\frac{\partial \omega_\mu}{\partial x_\nu} = \frac{\partial \omega_\nu}{\partial x_\mu}$ ist. Es ist also auch:
[-$\sum \frac{\partial a}{\partial x} x$-]
$\sum_\iota \frac{\partial a_{\mu\iota}}{\partial x_\nu} x_\iota = \sum_\iota \frac{\partial a_{\nu\iota}}{\partial x_\mu} x_\iota$
und daraus ergiebt sich mit Hülfe von (3'):
$\sum_{\iota\iota'} \frac{\partial a_{\mu\iota}}{\partial x_{\iota'}} x_\iota x_{\iota'} = \sum_{\iota\iota'} \frac{\partial a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_\mu} x_\iota x_{\iota'} = 0$
und [-woraus-] durch Integration der Differential-
gleichungen der kürzesten Linie:
(4). $\sum_\iota a_{\mu,\iota} x_\iota = \sum_\iota a^{(0)}_{\mu,\iota} x_\iota$
Bedeuten nun $t_{\iota\iota'} = t_{\iota',\iota}$ irgend welche Functionen
von $x_1, x_2, \ldots x_n$, welche mit ihren Ableitungen bis zur
dritten Ordnung einschließlich im Punkte 0 bestimmte
endliche Werthe haben, und besteht {+die+} [-eine-] identische
Gleichung [-...-]
$\sum_{\iota\iota'} t_{\iota\iota'} x_\iota x_{\iota'} = 0$

methods.what: Geodesic condition in new coordinates expressed via Christoffel-type combination p (sum of first-kind Christoffel symbols)
methods.quote: $p_{\mu,\iota,\iota'} = \frac{\partial a_{\iota\mu}}{\partial x_{\iota'}} + \frac{\partial a_{\iota'\mu}}{\partial x_\iota} - \frac{\partial a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_\mu}$

methods.what: Condition that radial lines are geodesics: quadratic form in p vanishes
Equivalent rewritten form of the geodesic condition
methods.quote: (3'.) $\sum_{\iota\iota'} \frac{\partial a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_\mu} x_\iota x_{\iota'} = 2 \sum_{\iota\iota'} \frac{\partial a_{\iota\mu}}{\partial x_{\iota'}} x_\iota x_{\iota'}$

methods.what: Introduction of auxiliary functions ω_μ and ω to rewrite (3')
Homogeneity argument: curl of ω is homogeneous of degree -1, hence vanishes if regular at 0
methods.quote: $f(tx_1, tx_2, \ldots tx_n) = t^{-1} f(x_1, x_2, \ldots x_n)$

methods.what: Resulting vanishing of radial derivative contractions of the metric
methods.quote: $\sum_{\iota\iota'} \frac{\partial a_{\mu\iota}}{\partial x_{\iota'}} x_\iota x_{\iota'} = \sum_{\iota\iota'} \frac{\partial a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_\mu} x_\iota x_{\iota'} = 0$

methods.what: Gauss lemma type result in normal coordinates: metric contracted with position equals its value at origin
